evals.prompt: Review evals/concision-and-logic/files/progress-note.md with the concision-and-logic skill before I send it to my supervisor.
evals.expected_output: Finds the logic faults the scanner cannot see (the scope shift from 3 nodes over 400 m to the 12 km route, the non sequitur from upload speed to hiker trust, the mixed-level list, the conclusion that restates the premise) and the wording tells it can (the breakdown preview, the hedge stack); returns a findings table and a revised note that claims only what was tested and keeps 3 nodes, 400 m and 2 s.
expectations: Flags 'Therefore the TrekLink mesh is ready for the 12 km Ta Xua route' as a scope shift or non sequitur and rewrites it to claim only what the 3-node, 400 m test showed
Flags 'so hikers will trust the app more' as unsupported and cuts it or marks it unverified, without inventing a survey, user count or figure to support it
Flags the Key outcomes list as mixing levels (a feature, a tool, a risk and a goal) and splits or regroups it
Cuts or replaces the closing 'In conclusion' sentence as a restated premise or recap, and removes the 'may potentially provide' hedge stack
Deletes the 'Here is a breakdown' line
Keeps 3 nodes, 400 m and 2 s unchanged and adds no new number
Returns a findings table followed by the revised text
Contains no em dash in the revised text

evals.prompt: Shorten evals/concision-and-logic/files/supervisor-email.md with the concision-and-logic skill. It goes to my supervisor today.
evals.expected_output: A revised email under 150 words whose first line after the greeting asks for the Report 3 extension from 14 to 21 November, with the late relay node (arrived 5 November) as the reason, no filler, and no invented detail about the robustness work.
expectations: The first sentence after the greeting asks for the one-week Report 3 extension from 14 November to 21 November
The revised email body, from greeting to sign-off, is under 150 words
Keeps the dates 5 November, 14 November and 21 November and the reason that the second relay node arrived late
Removes 'I hope this email finds you well', 'Please feel free to reach out' and the thank-you filler
Cuts 'improving the overall robustness of the system' and 'steady progress', or asks the writer for the specific change, without inventing what was improved
The subject line names Report 3 and the extension request
Contains no em dash

evals.prompt: Run the concision-and-logic scanner on evals/concision-and-logic/files/srs-paragraph.md and fix what it finds.
evals.expected_output: Runs draft_scan.py, reports the long aside, the low-severity '(configurable)' and the universal 'Every alert', fixes each without new facts, and leaves the abbreviation and the citation in parentheses as they are.
expectations: Runs scripts/draft_scan.py on the file and reports its findings
Rewrites the aside '(which the organiser can silence from the dashboard while a group is resting)' as its own sentence
Reports '(configurable)' as a short or low-severity parenthesis and folds it into the sentence, without adding a range or default the paragraph does not give
Flags 'Every alert is delivered to the organiser within 5 s' as an unsupported universal and narrows it or marks it unverified, without inventing a test result
Leaves '(SRS)' and '(Weber-Wulff et al., 2023)' unchanged
Keeps 15 min and 5 s unchanged

evals.prompt: My teammate pasted the Gemini answer in evals/concision-and-logic/files/gemini-answer.md to the question 'Which LoRa spreading factor did we choose for the relay nodes, and why?'. Tighten it with concision-and-logic so I can paste it in our team chat.
evals.expected_output: One to three sentences: SF9, because SF7 did not cover the 1.2 km gap between Node 3 and Node 4 in the 2 November range test. No options list, no preview line, no importance flag.
expectations: The first sentence gives the answer: SF9
Gives the reason with its evidence: SF7 did not cover the 1.2 km gap between Node 3 and Node 4 in the range test on 2 November
Removes the three unrequested options and the 'Here is a breakdown' line
Removes 'Great question', 'plays a crucial role', 'robust' and 'seamless'
The answer is 1 to 3 sentences long
Adds no fact that is not in the draft
Contains no em dash
